name: Dumbbell Deadlift
description: The dumbbell deadlift replicates the conventional deadlift pattern using two dumbbells instead of a barbell. Each dumbbell hangs at the sides of the thighs, allowing for a more neutral wrist position and a slightly narrower stance. It is an excellent entry point for learning the deadlift pattern, training at home without a barbell, or adding variety to posterior-chain programming.

execution.starting_position: Place two dumbbells on the floor at the sides of the feet. Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the dumbbells with palms facing the thighs.
execution.setup_instructions: Because each dumbbell is narrower than a barbell plate, you can stand in a narrower stance and the weight travels through a fuller range of motion if standing on a slight elevation.
steps: Step 1: Grip both dumbbells, ensuring a neutral spine and chest up.
Step 2: Brace the core and maintain lat engagement throughout.
Step 3: Drive through the floor, extending the hips and knees simultaneously.
Step 4: At lockout, stand fully erect with hips forward and shoulders back.
Step 5: Hinge back to lower the dumbbells under full control to the floor.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before each rep. Exhale as you stand up.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back at the start position
Letting the dumbbells drift forward away from the body
Not achieving full hip extension at lockout
safety_considerations: If using large-diameter dumbbells, the range of motion will be limited — use a step or platform to restore full ROM
Ensure a neutral spine before initiating the pull
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Floor to full lockout. Full hip and knee extension at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep dumbbells close — drag them up the legs
